new_candidates.body:
## Ticket type

Feature request / improvement

## Description

I want a Raspberry Pi 4 with 2 GB of RAM to control my SO-101 arm. The Pi will handle the arm, cameras, and tablet. A separate computer will handle the agent and model work.

I want to use LeRobot's low-level hardware APIs. The controller process should not load PyTorch. An import of `SO101Follower` reaches `lerobot_types.py`, which imports `torch`. The utility package also eagerly imports tensor-related helpers.

This is a concrete controller use case for #4693. That PR already passes the disconnected-controller check described below. It could provide the runtime fix for this issue. #4742 extends that work to teleoperation.

## Environment and reproduction

The reproduction on current `main` uses macOS arm64, Python 3.13.9, and LeRobot commit `146d8474932c8b566717eb2738ba459337ab71c4`. The Raspberry Pi motivates the request; the current-main reproduction uses a supported Python version on the Mac.

From a source checkout, create a separate environment without PyTorch:

```sh
uv venv --python 3.13 .venv-device
uv pip install --python .venv-device/bin/python \
  numpy==2.2.6 draccus==0.11.6 huggingface-hub==1.33.0 \
  pyserial==3.5 deepdiff==8.6.2 feetech-servo-sdk==1.0.0 \
  rustypot==1.13.1 tqdm==4.70.1 packaging==25.0
PYTHONPATH=src .venv-device/bin/python -c \
  'from lerobot.robots.so_follower import SO101Follower, SO101FollowerConfig'
```

The import fails through this chain:

```text
lerobot.robots.__init__
  -> lerobot.robots.robot
  -> lerobot.lerobot_types
  -> import torch
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'
```

## Expected behavior and checked result

The low-level controller API should import and construct a disconnected SO-101 follower without a PyTorch import. Tensor-dependent APIs should continue to load PyTorch when needed.

A separate smoke check loads six synthetic calibration entries and constructs the follower with a nonexistent serial path. The check blocks serial and native bus creation, then checks that the robot stays disconnected and `torch` stays absent.

- Current `main` at `146d8474`: fails during the import above.
- #4693 at `31d4686d`: passes the controller check in the same environment without PyTorch.

No physical arm movement is part of these checks. This evidence does not establish control timing or recording performance.

## Scope

This issue concerns runtime imports for the hardware API. The normal LeRobot installation still declares PyTorch as a required dependency. A supported hardware-only installation path remains a separate packaging question.

Codex helped prepare the reproduction and this report.
new_candidates.title: Support a Raspberry Pi SO-101 controller without PyTorch imports
